problem: The trap says a marker may be impossible in a sterile operating field, but skin fiducials are normally stuck on before the CT/MRI scan and stay on until surgery, so the student may think markers are placed during the sterile procedure.
fix: Say it clearly: fiducials must be on the skin before the scan and must not move afterwards; if they were never placed, or the skin surface shifts, the system falls back to surface matching or SLAM.

problem: The answer says the field geometry is tracked. In broadcast graphics the field or pitch model is pre-calibrated once; what is tracked live is the camera pose, and sometimes the ball or players.
fix: The camera pose (and often the ball or players) is tracked against a pre-calibrated model of the field; the system draws a line, player tag or statistic over the field; the display is the broadcast television feed.

problem: The standard textbook definition asks for three things: real plus virtual combined, registered in 3D, and interactive in real time. The answer drops the word interactive, which is the part examiners look for.
fix: Combine real and virtual; register the virtual object in 3D to the real world; run interactively in real time.
